name: graph-algorithms
summary: Exact classic graph algorithms (shortest path, topological sort, minimum spanning tree, max flow, graph coloring) exposed as an MCP server, each solved via one algorithm and independently checked via a second, structurally different one -- a Bellman-Ford recomputation for Dijkstra's shortest paths, the direct definition for Kahn's topological order (with a concrete cycle returned as proof when the graph isn't a DAG), the cycle-property exchange argument for Kruskal's minimum spanning tree, the max-flow min-cut theorem (a returned cut of equal capacity) for Edmonds-Karp's max flow, and the direct definition again for a DSATUR + forward-checking backtracking coloring solver, whose chromatic_number tool proves its minimum-colors answer with a clique lower bound plus exhaustive uncolorability at every smaller color count.
problem: Exact algorithmic reasoning over an explicit graph is a documented, actively-benchmarked LLM failure mode distinct from every other shape already in this collection: not sequential action search (strips-planner), not constraint satisfaction over a static assignment (logic-grid-solver), not a single calculation (secure-random/discrete-probability/time-arithmetic). Multiple 2025/2026 benchmarks built specifically to test this -- GraphArena, GraphOmni, GrAlgoBench, GTA, and 'Can Language Models Solve Graph Problems in Natural Language?' -- document accuracy dropping sharply on shortest-path, topological-sort, spanning-tree, and max-flow-style problems as graphs grow past a handful of nodes. No keyless MCP server was found exposing plain graph algorithms through a simple node/edge JSON vocabulary with an independent verifier; existing options found in this cycle's search require either full SMT-LIB/ASP formalization (mcp-solver) or a running Neo4j Graph Data Science instance (the GDS Agent paper), neither of which is a fixed-vocabulary, credential-free fit.
